units.title: Unit 77 — Verb or adjective + preposition
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 77. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Verb and adjective complementation; meaning contrasts
learningObjectives: Use common verb–preposition and adjective–preposition combinations accurately in context.
Distinguish prepositions that change the meaning of shout and throw.
Understand different uses of depend on, including uncertainty, financial reliance and trust.
Use correct structures such as complain to someone about something and translate into a language.
Apply the six additional preposition patterns explicitly practised in exercise 77.4.

items.pt: concordar com alguém
items.example: I agree with Maya about the new timetable.
items.note: Use agree with a person or opinion; disagree with is the opposite.

items.pt: preocupar-se com algo
items.example: Try not to worry about the test tomorrow.
items.note: Worry about a problem or possible event, not worry with it.

items.pt: estar satisfeito com algo
items.example: Our customers are satisfied with the service.
items.note: Satisfied with means pleased with a result or experience; note the preposition with.

items.pt: gastar dinheiro com algo
items.example: He spends too much money on takeaway food.
items.note: Spend money on a purchase or activity; use spend time doing something in another pattern.

items.pt: estar pensando em fazer algo; considerar fazer algo
items.example: I am thinking of learning Italian next year.
items.note: The book teaches be thinking of + -ing to express a plan under consideration; not thinking of to do.

items.pt: pertencer a alguém
items.example: That blue backpack belongs to my sister.
items.note: Belong to indicates ownership or membership; never belong with a person.

items.pt: traduzir para; verter para outro idioma
items.example: They translated the instructions into Spanish.
items.note: Translate a text into the target language; the original text may be translated from another language.

items.pt: reclamar a alguém; fazer uma reclamação a alguém
items.example: She complained to the receptionist about the noise.
items.note: The person receiving the complaint follows to; the problem commonly follows about.

items.pt: reclamar de algo; queixar-se de algo
items.example: Several passengers complained about the delay.
items.note: Use about for the subject of a complaint, and to for the person receiving it.

items.pt: concentrar-se em algo
items.example: I cannot concentrate on my reading with that music playing.
items.note: Concentrate on a task or subject; on is required in this pattern.

items.pt: contar com alguém; confiar em alguém
items.example: We can rely on Daniel to finish his part of the work.
items.note: Rely on means trust someone or something to work or help as expected.

items.pt: depender de algo; estar condicionado a algo
items.example: Whether we go cycling depends on the weather.
items.note: Contingency: the outcome is determined by a condition. Not depend of.

items.pt: depender financeiramente de alguém
items.example: While he was studying, Leo depended on his parents for money.
items.note: Need financial support from someone; use depend on a person for a particular resource.

items.pt: contar com o apoio de alguém; depender do apoio de alguém
items.example: You can depend on your colleagues for support during the project.
items.note: Reliability: trust that someone will provide help or support when needed.

items.pt: gritar para alguém ouvir; chamar alguém em voz alta
items.example: I shouted to Nora across the playground so she could hear me.
items.note: Shout to someone to be heard, often from a distance; the intention is not necessarily anger.

items.pt: gritar com alguém; dar uma bronca em alguém
items.example: The coach shouted at us because we were not listening.
items.note: Shout at someone usually suggests anger or criticism, unlike calling to someone.

items.pt: jogar algo para alguém pegar
items.example: Can you throw the keys to me from the balcony?
items.note: Throw to someone so they can catch or receive it.

items.pt: arremessar algo contra alguém; jogar algo visando atingir alguém
items.example: The child threw a cushion at his brother during the argument.
items.note: Throw at someone or something with the intention of hitting a target.

items.pt: ser bom em algo; ter habilidade em algo
items.example: My cousin is good at solving puzzles.
items.note: Good at + noun or -ing indicates ability; opposite: bad at.

items.pt: ser ruim em algo; não ter habilidade em algo
items.example: I am bad at remembering people’s birthdays.
items.note: Opposite of good at; use at before a noun or -ing form.

items.pt: ter medo de algo
items.example: My friend is afraid of flying.
items.note: Afraid of + noun or -ing expresses fear; not afraid from.

items.pt: gostar muito de alguém; ter carinho por alguém
items.example: Her grandparents are very fond of her.
items.note: Fond of indicates affection or liking; it may also refer to an activity.

items.pt: ser semelhante a algo; parecer-se com algo
items.example: This jacket is similar to the one I bought last year.
items.note: Similar to means alike in some ways, not necessarily identical.

items.pt: ser diferente de algo
items.example: Life in a small village is different from life in a city.
items.note: The book uses different from; contrast with similar to.

items.pt: ter interesse em algo; estar interessado em algo
items.example: She is interested in wildlife photography.
items.note: Interested in + noun or -ing; use in rather than on or about here.

items.pt: estar ciente de algo; ter consciência de algo
items.example: The team is aware of the safety problem.
items.note: To know that a problem or situation exists; often followed by of.

items.pt: estar cansado ou farto de algo
items.example: I am tired of waiting for a reply.
items.note: Tired of + noun or -ing means bored or annoyed by repetition; differs from physically tired.

items.pt: ser louco por alguém; gostar muito de alguém
items.example: Ellie is mad about the singer from that band.
items.note: Informal British use: like a person or activity very much; not the angry meaning of mad.

items.pt: estar com pouco de algo; estar em falta de algo
items.example: We are short of milk, so I will stop at the shop.
items.note: Have less than you need; often used for money, time, supplies or food.

items.pt: errado com; haver algo de errado com
items.example: There is something wrong with the printer.
items.note: Usually used as something wrong with ... or what is wrong with ...?

items.pt: gostar muito de algo; ser entusiasta de algo
items.example: My uncle is keen on growing vegetables.
items.note: British English: like or be enthusiastic about something; from exercise 77.4.

items.pt: sofrer de algo; padecer de algo
items.example: He suffers from hay fever every spring.
items.note: Commonly used for an illness or ongoing problem; from exercise 77.4.

items.pt: conseguir fazer algo; ter êxito em algo
items.example: She succeeded in passing the exam on her second attempt.
items.note: Succeed in + -ing, not succeed to + infinitive; from exercise 77.4.

items.pt: casar-se com alguém
items.example: His sister is going to get married to Alex in June.
items.note: Get married to a person; the wedding may happen in a place. From exercise 77.4.

items.pt: candidatar-se a algo; solicitar algo
items.example: I plan to apply for the internship next month.
items.note: Apply for a job, position or benefit; apply to an organisation. From exercise 77.4.

items.pt: pedir desculpas por algo
items.example: He apologised for arriving late.
items.note: Apologise for + noun or -ing; apologise to a person. From exercise 77.4.

sectionsChecked: A: Verb + preposition and special language-help box on three uses of depend on
B: Illustrated contrasts shout to/at and throw to/at
C: Adjective + preposition combinations, informal register and opposites

units.title: Unit 78 — Prepositional phrases
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 78. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Fixed prepositional expressions and meaning contrasts
learningObjectives: Use fixed by, on and in prepositional phrases naturally and with the correct noun.
Distinguish accidental from intentional events using by accident and on purpose.
Contrast on time with in time, and in the end with at the end.
Express business travel, currency of information and the present moment with idiomatic phrases.
Apply the spelling and grammar of out-of-date, up-to-date and in future, as checked in the exercises.

items.pt: por engano; sem querer
items.example: I picked up your coat by mistake after the meeting.
items.note: Used when you accidentally do the wrong thing because of an error; not on mistake.

items.pt: à mão; manualmente
items.example: The invitations were written by hand.
items.note: Made or done without using machinery for the main work.

items.pt: por acaso; casualmente
items.example: I met an old school friend by chance at the station.
items.note: An unplanned meeting or event; close in meaning to accidentally in some contexts.

items.pt: por acidente; sem querer
items.example: She knocked over the glass by accident.
items.note: Unintentional; contrast with on purpose, which is intentional.

items.pt: de propósito; intencionalmente
items.example: He left the door open on purpose to let in some fresh air.
items.note: Deliberately, not by accident; on is required.

items.pt: ao telefone; falando ao telefone
items.example: Can I call you later? I am on the phone.
items.note: Speaking or communicating by telephone at that moment.

items.pt: em greve
items.example: The bus drivers are on strike over working conditions.
items.note: Refusing to work collectively as a protest, often about pay or working conditions.

items.pt: em exposição; exposto para o público
items.example: Several local paintings are on display in the library.
items.note: Placed where people can look at them, often in a shop, gallery or exhibition.

items.pt: em chamas; pegando fogo
items.example: The old shed was on fire when the firefighters arrived.
items.note: Burning; often used with be or catch.

items.pt: a bordo; dentro de um veículo de transporte
items.example: All passengers must be on board before the ferry leaves.
items.note: On or inside a ship, plane, train or similar means of transport.

items.pt: com pressa; apressado
items.example: I cannot stop to chat because I am in a hurry.
items.note: Needing to do something or go somewhere quickly; not on a hurry.

items.pt: em detalhe; detalhadamente
items.example: The engineer explained the procedure in detail.
items.note: Giving all relevant or important information rather than only a summary.

items.pt: daqui para frente; no futuro; de agora em diante
items.example: In future, please check the address before sending the parcel.
items.note: British English: from now onwards; can be different from in the future, which may refer to an unspecified later time.

items.pt: em lágrimas; chorando
items.example: The little boy was in tears after losing his favourite toy.
items.note: Crying; use in, not on or with, in this expression.

items.pt: na hora certa; pontualmente
items.example: The train arrived on time at nine o’clock.
items.note: Punctual: at the scheduled or expected time; not the same as in time.

items.pt: a tempo; antes que seja tarde
items.example: We reached the cinema in time to buy tickets before the film started.
items.note: Early enough for something to happen or to avoid being late for an event.

items.pt: no fim das contas; finalmente; por fim
items.example: We tried several shops, but in the end we ordered online.
items.note: Finally, after events, discussion or difficulty; not the physical ending of a book.

items.pt: no final de algo; na parte final de algo
items.example: There is a short quiz at the end of the chapter.
items.note: Refers to the last part or point of a time period, event, story or object.
items.speechText: at the end of the chapter

items.pt: no mundo dos negócios; atuando comercialmente
items.example: Building trust is important when you work in business.
items.note: Refers to business activity or the commercial world; distinct from on business.

items.pt: a trabalho; em viagem de negócios
items.example: My manager is in Lisbon on business this week.
items.note: Travelling or staying somewhere for work rather than for a holiday.

items.pt: desatualizado; antiquado; obsoleto
items.example: Some information in this guide is out-of-date.
items.note: No longer current or accurate; the book uses hyphens in the written form.

items.pt: atualizado; em dia; com informações recentes
items.example: Make sure the safety instructions are up-to-date.
items.note: Including the most recent changes or information; opposite of out-of-date.

items.pt: manter-se atualizado sobre algo; acompanhar novidades sobre algo
items.example: I read the weekly newsletter to keep up-to-date with industry news.
items.note: Keep informed about the latest developments; with introduces the topic.
items.speechText: keep up to date with something

items.pt: daqui a pouco; em um instante
items.example: I will be with you in a moment.
items.note: Very soon, not now; differs from at the moment.

items.pt: daqui a pouco; em um minutinho
items.example: I just need to finish this message; I will join you in a minute.
items.note: A casual synonym of in a moment; does not always mean exactly sixty seconds.

items.pt: no momento; agora
items.example: The receptionist is busy at the moment.
items.note: Now, at the present time; not in the moment in this meaning.

items.pt: agora mesmo; neste exato momento
items.example: I cannot speak right now because I am in a meeting.
items.note: At this very moment; a common alternative to at the moment.

sectionsChecked: A: By/on/in + noun expressions, illustrated accident/purpose contrast
B: Easily confused prepositional phrases and common mistake concerning at the moment
